s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac arrest with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and hemodynamic collapse
salient_findings: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: 34-year-old White woman with a history of obesity
Presented after an unwitnessed cardiac arrest
Required mechanical intubation for airway protection
Developed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
Experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions
Troponin T: 0.847 µg/L (elevated)
Troponin I: 0.13 ng/mL (elevated)
Urine toxicology, alcohol, and acetaminophen screening results were negative
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with heart rate 101 beats/min, QTc 443 ms
Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal biventricular size and function
Diagnostic coronary angiogram: no obstructive coronary artery disease
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging: mild left ventricular and left atrial dilation, preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (62%)
Electroencephalogram showed status epilepticus

shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular fibrillation with no clear underlying cause

shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, which can be associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although not directly implicated, it is a common cause of sudden cardiac death and ventricular tachycardia in young adults
